matched_question.prompt: Explain how a Hash Map handles collisions and the significance of the load factor.

transcripts.raw_spoken: a hash map never has collisions because the hash function always gives a unique index for every key
transcripts.corrected: a hash map never has collisions because the hash function always gives a unique index for every key

where_got_wrong.error: The candidate stated that hash maps never experience collisions. In reality, due to the pigeonhole principle, any hash function mapping a large keyspace to a smaller array index space will produce collisions, which must be handled explicitly.
where_got_wrong.candidate_quote: a hash map never has collisions because the hash function always gives a unique index for every key

rubric_idea_breakdown.criterion: Hash collisions occur when distinct keys produce identical hash indices, resolved via separate chaining (linked lists/trees) or open addressing (probing).
rubric_idea_breakdown.reasoning: The candidate incorrectly claimed that a hash map never has collisions due to a unique index for every key, failing to mention collision resolution mechanisms like chaining or open addressing.

rubric_idea_breakdown.criterion: Load factor is the ratio of stored elements to total bucket capacity (N / C), indicating table density.
rubric_idea_breakdown.reasoning: The candidate made no mention of the load factor, its formula (N / C), or its role in indicating table density.

rubric_idea_breakdown.criterion: Exceeding the maximum load factor triggers resizing and rehashing of all entries into a larger array (usually 2x) to maintain amortized O(1) lookups.
rubric_idea_breakdown.reasoning: The candidate did not mention resizing, rehashing, or load factor thresholds.

actionable_feedback.issue: Incorrectly claimed that hash maps do not have collisions.
actionable_feedback.evidence_quote: a hash map never has collisions because the hash function always gives a unique index for every key
actionable_feedback.why_it_matters: Collisions are inevitable in hash maps when distinct keys hash to the same index, requiring specific resolution strategies.
actionable_feedback.improvement_action: Explain how separate chaining or open addressing handles multiple keys mapping to the same bucket.
actionable_feedback.example_sentence: Hash collisions happen when two different keys generate the same hash value, so we use chaining or probing to resolve them.

actionable_feedback.issue: Omitted any explanation of the load factor.
actionable_feedback.why_it_matters: The load factor measures how full the hash table is and dictates when resizing is required to preserve O(1) performance.
actionable_feedback.improvement_action: Define the load factor as the ratio of stored elements to total capacity.
actionable_feedback.example_sentence: The load factor is the ratio of elements to buckets, indicating when the table needs to grow.

actionable_feedback.issue: Omitted the process of resizing and rehashing.
actionable_feedback.why_it_matters: Resizing maintains efficient operations by preventing excessive collisions as the table fills up.
actionable_feedback.improvement_action: Describe how exceeding the maximum load factor triggers array expansion and rehashing.
actionable_feedback.example_sentence: When the load factor exceeds the threshold, we resize the array and rehash all entries.
